quests.hint: Suggest a fair system with 'Shall we…?' and give a concrete offer to make it real.
quests.explanation: 'Shall we…?' proposes a plan without giving orders. Offering specific days shows you're willing to do your part, which makes it easier for the roommate to agree.
quests.situationText: Dishes are piling up in the shared flat, and you and your roommate both feel a little annoyed. You'd like a simple system that feels fair.
quests.sampleAnswer: Shall we take turns doing the dishes? I could do Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: Shall we take turns doing the dishes? I'll do Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
acceptedSynonyms: Shall we take turns doing the dishes? I'll do Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
What if we take turns with the dishes? I can take Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
How about we split the dishes? I'll do three days and you do four.
Why don't we make a schedule for the dishes? I'll take Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

quests.hint: Ask a parent for permission with the reason and time. Make it easy for them to say yes.
quests.explanation: Parents want to know who, when, and why. Giving all three in the first breath, including 'we're working on a project', prevents a list of follow-up questions.
quests.situationText: You'd like your classmate Jake to stay overnight at your family home on Saturday so you can finish a school project. You ask your mother in the kitchen.
quests.sampleAnswer: Mum, is it okay if Jake stays over on Saturday? We need to finish our project.
quests.correctAnswer: Mum, is it okay if Jake stays over on Saturday? We're working on a project.
acceptedSynonyms: Can Jake sleep over on Saturday, Mum? We have a project to finish.
Would it be all right if Jake stayed here on Saturday night? We have a project due.
Mum, is it okay if Jake stays over on Saturday? We're working on a project.
Mum, would you mind if Jake stayed over on Saturday? It's for a school project.

quests.hint: Ask before you use someone's food and promise to replace it. That's what makes it fair.
quests.explanation: Sharing a kitchen works on trust. 'I'll buy more tomorrow' shows respect for their property and reduces the chance of tension.
quests.situationText: You come home late and you're hungry. There's only your roommate's leftover pasta in the fridge, and she's still awake in the living room.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hey, is it okay if I finish your pasta? I'll buy more tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: Is it okay if I have some of your pasta? I'll buy more tomorrow.
acceptedSynonyms: Is it okay if I have some of your pasta? I'll buy more tomorrow.
Would you mind if I ate some of your pasta? I'll replace it tomorrow.
Can I have a bit of your leftover pasta? I'll get some more tomorrow.
Sorry, I'm starving. Can I eat your pasta if I replace it tomorrow?

quests.hint: On a work call, ask for the person by name and use 'Could I speak to…?'
quests.explanation: 'Could I speak to…?' is the standard opening for calling a workplace. It's polite, neutral, and lets the receptionist connect you without asking what you want.
quests.situationText: You dial the main number of an insurance company. A receptionist answers and you need to talk to Ms. Reid, who handled your case.
quests.sampleAnswer: Good morning, I'm trying to reach Ms. Reid. Is she available?
quests.correctAnswer: Hello, could I speak to Ms. Reid, please?
acceptedSynonyms: Hi, is Ms. Reid available, please?
Good morning, may I speak with Ms. Reid?
Hello, could I speak to Ms. Reid, please?
Hello, I'd like to talk to Ms. Reid, please.

quests.hint: If the person isn't there, leave a clear message: who you are, what to do, and your number.
quests.explanation: A useful message contains your name, what you want the person to do, and how to reach you. 'Please ask her to call' is a polite way to give a small instruction.
quests.situationText: The receptionist says Ms. Reid is in a meeting. You'd like her to call back. Your name is Daniel and your number is 555-0142.
quests.sampleAnswer: That's okay. Could you ask her to call Daniel back on 555-0142?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you take a message? Please ask her to call Daniel back on 555-0142.
acceptedSynonyms: Could you take a message? Please ask her to call Daniel back on 555-0142.
Could you please ask her to call me back? It's Daniel, 555-0142.
Yes, could you tell her that Daniel called and ask her to ring me on 555-0142?
Could I leave a message, please? Just ask her to call Daniel at 555-0142.

quests.hint: At a clinic, give your full name and the purpose of the call at the beginning. Don't wait for questions.
quests.explanation: Reception staff deal with many callers. 'This is…, I'm calling about…' is the standard structure to get to the point quickly, and gives them what they need to find your record.
quests.situationText: You need to check your appointment time for tomorrow. The clinic's receptionist has just picked up the phone. Your name is Ana Silva.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, it's Ana Silva here. I'm phoning to check my appointment for tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: Hello, this is Ana Silva. I'm calling about my appointment tomorrow.
acceptedSynonyms: Hi, it's Ana Silva here. I'm phoning to check my appointment for tomorrow.
Good morning, this is Ana Silva calling. I'd like to confirm my appointment tomorrow.
Hello, this is Ana Silva. I'm calling about my appointment tomorrow.
Hello, I'm Ana Silva, and I'm calling to ask about my appointment tomorrow.

quests.hint: Apologize for the mistake and confirm who you're talking to. Don't just hang up.
quests.explanation: If you dial the wrong number, checking the name of the place helps you see whether it was you or the number. 'I think I've got the wrong number' is more polite than blaming the other person.
quests.situationText: You call what you think is the Green Dental Clinic, but the person answering seems confused. It might not be the right number.
quests.sampleAnswer: Oh, sorry. I think I have the wrong number. Is this Green Dental Clinic?
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, I think I've got the wrong number. Is this the Green Dental Clinic?
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry, is this Green Dental Clinic? I may have dialed the wrong number.
Oh, I'm sorry. I was trying to reach Green Dental Clinic. Have I got the right number?
Sorry to bother you. Is this Green Dental Clinic, or have I dialed the wrong number?
Sorry, I think I've got the wrong number. Is this the Green Dental Clinic?

quests.hint: Tell them the problem and your plan. It's much better than saying 'hello?' until the call ends.
quests.explanation: 'The line is breaking up' explains what's happening, and 'I'll call you back' gives a plan so the other person isn't left confused.
quests.situationText: You're talking to your friend while walking through a tunnel, and the signal keeps dropping. You want to solve it.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, the line's breaking up. I'll hang up and call you back in a minute.
quests.correctAnswer: The line is breaking up. I'll hang up and call you back in a minute.
acceptedSynonyms: I can't hear you well. I'll call you back in a minute.
The line is breaking up. I'll hang up and call you back in a minute.
You keep cutting out. Let me call you back once I have a better signal.
Sorry, the signal's terrible here. I'll ring you back in a minute.

quests.hint: When answering for someone else, say they aren't available and offer to help.
quests.explanation: 'I'm afraid' softens bad news, and offering to take a message keeps the call useful. This also shows that the caller isn't being ignored.
quests.situationText: You answer the office phone. The caller asks for your colleague Sara, but she has just left for a meeting.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello. I'm afraid Sara isn't here at the moment. Can I take a message?
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid she's not here right now. Can I take a message?
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry, Sara has just stepped out. Would you like to leave a message?
She's away from her desk at the moment. Can I pass on a message?
I'm sorry, she's in a meeting right now. Shall I take your details?
I'm afraid she's not here right now. Can I take a message?

quests.hint: Give landmarks for your location, and give them in order of how easy they are to see.
quests.explanation: Couriers can't see your building, so tell them what they'll notice: a door color and a neighboring shop. That's more useful than repeating the address.
quests.situationText: A courier calls because he's on your street but can't find your building. Yours has a green door and is next to a pharmacy.
quests.sampleAnswer: It's the one with the green door, beside the pharmacy.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm in the building with the green door, next to the pharmacy.
acceptedSynonyms: It's the one with the green door, beside the pharmacy.
Look for the pharmacy. I'm in the building next to it, with a green door.
I'm in the building with the green door, next to the pharmacy.
My building is next to the pharmacy. It has a green door.

quests.hint: Report a late delivery with the facts: what, when it was due, and the tracking number.
quests.explanation: Customer service staff need to identify your order quickly. The due date and the tracking number are the two facts that let them start the search.
quests.situationText: You ordered a coat online and it was supposed to arrive yesterday. Nothing has come, and you're calling the delivery company. You have the tracking number. The tracking number is 4471.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, my parcel was supposed to come yesterday, but it hasn't arrived. The tracking number is 4471.
quests.correctAnswer: My parcel was due yesterday, but it hasn't come. Can I give you the tracking number?
acceptedSynonyms: My parcel was due yesterday, but it hasn't come. Can I give you the tracking number?
My order should have been delivered yesterday, but it hasn't arrived. I have the tracking number here.
I'm calling about a parcel that was due yesterday. It still hasn't come. Can you check the tracking number?
There's a problem with my delivery. It was due yesterday and it hasn't turned up. I can give you the tracking number.

quests.hint: Explain why the default doesn't work, then suggest an alternative.
quests.explanation: 'I won't be home' is the reason and 'leave it with reception' is the solution. Giving both means the courier doesn't have to invent a plan.
quests.situationText: The courier tells you he'll deliver at 2 p.m., but you'll be at work. Your building has a reception desk that's staffed all day.
quests.sampleAnswer: I won't be home at two. Could you leave it at the reception desk?
quests.correctAnswer: I won't be home at that time. Could you leave it with the reception desk?
acceptedSynonyms: I'll be at work then. Is it possible to leave the parcel at reception?
Nobody will be home at two, but reception is open all day. Could you leave it there?
I won't be home at that time. Could you leave it with the reception desk?
I can't be there at that time. Would you mind leaving it with the front desk?

quests.hint: Ask about the bag by describing its size or type. Airlines have strict rules, so check before you fly.
quests.explanation: Check-in staff answer questions on hand luggage all day. Pointing to the bag and asking 'Can I take this…?' is enough, and you avoid an expensive surprise at the gate.
quests.situationText: You're at the airline's check-in counter with a medium-sized backpack. You'd like to keep it with you on the plane.
quests.sampleAnswer: Is this bag small enough to take on the plane with me?
quests.correctAnswer: Can I take this bag on board as hand luggage?
acceptedSynonyms: Is this bag small enough to take on the plane with me?
Sorry, would this count as hand luggage, or do I have to check it?
Am I allowed to carry this backpack on board?
Can I take this bag on board as hand luggage?

quests.hint: Two related questions about the same thing can be linked with 'and'. Ask about the time and the storage.
quests.explanation: Before leaving a hostel you should ask both when you must leave and what to do with your bag. Asking both saves a second trip to reception.
quests.situationText: You're staying at a hostel and your flight leaves in the evening. Tomorrow you'll need to check out in the morning but you'll explore the city first.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, what time do I need to check out? And could I keep my bag here until the evening?
quests.correctAnswer: What time is check-out, and can I leave my bag here afterwards?
acceptedSynonyms: When do I need to check out? Could I keep my luggage here until the evening?
What time is check-out, and can I leave my bag here afterwards?
Could you tell me the check-out time, and whether you can store my bag after that?
What time do I have to leave the room, and can my bag stay here for the day?

quests.hint: For public transport, ask about the last service. 'The last…' is a useful phrase for evening plans.
quests.explanation: 'The last bus' is a fixed phrase, and asking about it protects you from being stranded. Adding 'tonight' makes clear you mean today's timetable.
quests.situationText: You've been at a party near the city center, and you're planning to take the bus to the airport for an early flight. You ask a station attendant when the service ends.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, when does the final airport bus go this evening?
quests.correctAnswer: What time is the last bus to the airport tonight?
acceptedSynonyms: Could you tell me when the last bus to the airport leaves tonight?
Sorry, when does the final airport bus go this evening?
Do you know what time the last bus to the airport is tonight?
What time is the last bus to the airport tonight?

quests.hint: Say what you want to send, where, and ask about the time. A second question is natural.
quests.explanation: Post office clerks can process a parcel fastest when they know the destination. 'How long will it take?' is a sensible follow-up about delivery time.
quests.situationText: You're at the post office with a small box for a friend who lives in Canada.
quests.sampleAnswer: I need to send this box to Canada. How many days does it usually take?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to send this parcel to Canada. How long will it take?
acceptedSynonyms: I need to send this box to Canada. How many days does it usually take?
I'd like to send this parcel to Canada. How long will it take?
Could I send this parcel to Canada, please? When will it arrive?
How long would it take for this parcel to get to Canada?

quests.hint: A top-up needs an amount. Name the phone service or number if you're asked.
quests.explanation: Shop assistants need the service and the amount. Specifying the amount first makes the transaction quick.
quests.situationText: You're in a phone shop because your prepaid credit ran out. You want to add twenty euros.
quests.sampleAnswer: Can I add twenty euros of credit to my phone?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to top up my phone with twenty euros, please.
acceptedSynonyms: Can I add twenty euros of credit to my phone?
I need to put twenty euros on my prepaid phone, please.
Could you top up my number with twenty euros?
I'd like to top up my phone with twenty euros, please.

quests.hint: Ask for the exchange rate before you commit. 'What's the rate today?' is a standard question.
quests.explanation: Exchange rates change daily, so asking first is sensible. Saying the amount you're exchanging helps the cashier calculate.
quests.situationText: You've just arrived in a new country and you're at a bank counter. You want to exchange a hundred dollars for local money.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, I'd like to change a hundred dollars into local currency. What's the rate today?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to change some money into local currency. What's the rate today?
acceptedSynonyms: Could I exchange a hundred dollars, please? What rate are you offering today?
I'd like to change some money into local currency. What's the rate today?
I want to change a hundred dollars. What's today's exchange rate?
Can you tell me today's rate for dollars? I'd like to change a hundred.

quests.hint: Say what happened in simple words: 'locked out' is the phrase for keys inside. Then ask for the solution.
quests.explanation: 'I've locked myself out' is a fixed phrase everyone recognizes. Asking for a spare key goes straight to the practical fix.
quests.situationText: You've just shut your apartment door and realize your keys are inside. The building manager is in the lobby.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, my keys are inside my flat. Is there a spare set anywhere?
quests.correctAnswer: I've locked myself out. Do you have a spare key?
acceptedSynonyms: I've locked myself out. Do you have a spare key?
Sorry, my keys are inside my flat. Is there a spare set anywhere?
I've shut my keys inside. Could you let me in, please?
I'm locked out of my apartment. Can you help me get in?

quests.hint: Explain the mistake clearly with numbers. Numbers keep the conversation about facts, not feelings.
quests.explanation: 'I gave you a twenty, not a ten' is a precise fact the cashier can check. It keeps the mood calm because you're describing, not blaming.
quests.situationText: You paid for a snack with a twenty-euro note, but the cashier gave you change for a ten. You spot it right away.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, I think there's a mistake with my change. I handed you a twenty.
quests.correctAnswer: I think you gave me the wrong change. I gave you a twenty, not a ten.
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry, I think there's a mistake with my change. I handed you a twenty.
Could you check my change, please? I paid with a twenty, not a ten.
I think you gave me the wrong change. I gave you a twenty, not a ten.
Excuse me, I gave you twenty euros, but this is change for ten.

quests.hint: Explain the emergency, then give two options so the other person can choose what's easiest.
quests.explanation: Offering two options ('use your phone, or charge mine') gives a stranger an easy way to help. Explaining the urgency makes the request feel fair.
quests.situationText: It's raining, your phone is dead, and you need to call a taxi. You step into a small shop and speak to the owner.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sorry, my phone died and I need a taxi. Could I use yours, or charge mine for a few minutes?
quests.correctAnswer: My phone's dead and I need to call a taxi. Could I use your phone, or charge mine for a few minutes?
acceptedSynonyms: My phone's dead and I need to call a taxi. Could I use your phone, or charge mine for a few minutes?
My battery's gone and I have to call a taxi. Is it possible to charge my phone here for a bit?
Could I make a quick call from your phone? Mine's out of battery and I need a taxi.
Sorry to bother you, but my phone has died. Would you mind if I charged it while I wait for a taxi?

quests.hint: Describe the symptom and how long you've had it, then ask for advice.
quests.explanation: Pharmacists advise quickly when they know the symptom and its length. 'What would you recommend?' asks for expertise rather than a specific product.
quests.situationText: You have had a sore throat for two days and you'd like to try something from the pharmacy before seeing a doctor.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've got a sore throat that started two days ago. Is there something you'd suggest?
quests.correctAnswer: I've had a sore throat for two days. What would you recommend?
acceptedSynonyms: My throat has been sore for a couple of days. Is there anything you'd suggest?
I have a sore throat that won't go away. What could I take?
I've had a sore throat for two days. What would you recommend?
Could you recommend something for a sore throat? It's been two days.

quests.hint: Give the doctor's name, appointment time, and tell reception you're new.
quests.explanation: New patients may need to fill in forms, so saying 'first time' lets reception prepare. The doctor's name and time help them find you in the system.
quests.situationText: You walk into a clinic for the first time. Your appointment with Dr. Kaya is at ten o'clock.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, I'm here to see Dr. Kaya at ten. I'm a new patient.
quests.correctAnswer: I have an appointment with Dr. Kaya at 10. It's my first time here.
acceptedSynonyms: I have an appointment with Dr. Kaya at 10. It's my first time here.
Hi, I'm here to see Dr. Kaya at ten. I'm a new patient.
Good morning. I have a ten o'clock appointment with Dr. Kaya, and I haven't been here before.
I'm here for my appointment with Dr. Kaya at ten. I'm new here.

quests.hint: Ask about dose and food together. Both are common safety questions.
quests.explanation: 'How often' and 'with food' are the two questions pharmacists expect. Asking them shows you want to use the medicine correctly.
quests.situationText: The pharmacist has given you a box of tablets for a stomach problem, but the instructions on the box are too small to read.
quests.sampleAnswer: Thank you. How often should I take these? Should I take them with food?
quests.correctAnswer: How often should I take these tablets, and should I take them with food?
acceptedSynonyms: Could you tell me how many of these to take each day, and whether I should eat first?
How many times a day should I take these? Do they have to be taken with a meal?
How often should I take these tablets, and should I take them with food?
Sorry, could you explain the dose? How often, and with or without food?

quests.hint: Describe the problem, when it started, and ask for action. Facts help the landlord decide how urgent it is.
quests.explanation: 'Since yesterday' gives the landlord a timeline. Asking for someone to come 'and look at it' is a practical request, not an accusation.
quests.situationText: The tap in your rented kitchen has been dripping non-stop since yesterday. You're calling your landlord.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, there's a problem with the kitchen tap. It's been dripping since yesterday. Can you send someone?
quests.correctAnswer: The kitchen tap has been leaking since yesterday. Could someone come and look at it?
acceptedSynonyms: Hi, there's a problem with the kitchen tap. It's been dripping since yesterday. Can you send someone?
The tap in my kitchen is leaking. Could you arrange for someone to fix it?
I'm calling because the kitchen tap hasn't stopped leaking since yesterday. When could someone come?
The kitchen tap has been leaking since yesterday. Could someone come and look at it?

quests.hint: With technical support, say what you've already tried. It stops the agent from suggesting the obvious.
quests.explanation: Saying 'I've already restarted the router' saves time because that's the first thing support agents suggest. It shows you've tried and helps them go straight to the next step.
quests.situationText: Your internet keeps disconnecting every few minutes. You call your provider's helpline and you've already switched the router off and on.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, my internet keeps dropping out every few minutes. I've already restarted the router.
quests.correctAnswer: My internet keeps disconnecting every few minutes. I've already restarted the router.
acceptedSynonyms: I'm having trouble with my connection. It drops every few minutes, and restarting the router didn't help.
My internet keeps disconnecting every few minutes. I've already restarted the router.
The wifi disconnects again and again. I've tried switching the router off and on.
Hi, my internet cuts out every few minutes. I've already tried restarting the router.

quests.hint: Introduce yourself by location, describe what you see, and ask a direct question.
quests.explanation: Beginning with 'I'm from the flat below' explains why you're at their door. A calm description of the leak, followed by a question, invites cooperation instead of blame.
quests.situationText: Water is dripping through your bathroom ceiling. You go upstairs and ring the doorbell of the flat above. A man opens the door.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, I live in the flat below. Water's coming through my ceiling. Is your bathroom leaking?
quests.correctAnswer: Hi, I'm from the flat below. Water is coming through my ceiling. Is your bathroom leaking?
acceptedSynonyms: Sorry to disturb you. I live downstairs and there's water coming through my bathroom ceiling. Have you noticed a leak?
Hello, I'm your neighbor from below. There's water dripping from my ceiling. Could you check your bathroom?
Excuse me, water is coming into my flat from above. Do you know if something is leaking up here?
Hi, I'm from the flat below. Water is coming through my ceiling. Is your bathroom leaking?

quests.hint: You need two things from one person, so state both. Your first question sets the location.
quests.explanation: Combining a request for a recommendation and directions is realistic; you rarely need only one piece of information. Saying 'cheap' and 'near here' narrows the answer.
quests.situationText: You've just arrived in a new city and stop at the tourist information desk. You want a cheap place for lunch nearby and need to know how to get there.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hi, could you recommend somewhere cheap for lunch near here? And how do I get there?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you recommend a cheap place for lunch near here, and tell me how to get there?
acceptedSynonyms: Could you suggest an inexpensive place to have lunch around here, and how to walk there?
Could you recommend a cheap place for lunch near here, and tell me how to get there?
I'm looking for a cheap lunch place nearby. Can you recommend one, and show me the way?
Do you know a good, cheap place for lunch nearby? How would I get there?

quests.hint: You don't know this shop's return rules, so ask about them. A 'do I…or can I…?' question covers both options at once.
quests.explanation: Rather than assuming, 'Do I need to…or can I…?' asks about both options. It shows you're willing to follow the rules and lets staff explain the correct procedure.
quests.situationText: You ordered shoes online from a shop that also has a physical store in your town. They don't fit, and you want to return them.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, I'd like to return the shoes I ordered online. Do I have to post them, or can I bring them to the shop?
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to return the shoes I bought online. Do I need to post them, or can I bring them in?
acceptedSynonyms: I ordered these shoes online and they don't fit. Can I return them here in the shop, or must I mail them back?
Could you tell me how to return shoes bought online? Can I do it in the store?
Sorry, the shoes I got online don't fit. Do I send them back, or can I drop them off here?
I'd like to return the shoes I bought online. Do I need to post them, or can I bring them in?

quests.hint: Give the change you want and the reason. Suggest a specific time so they can say yes or no.
quests.explanation: Delivery rescheduling is easier when you state both the day and the time slot you prefer. The reason ('I won't be home') shows the change is necessary.
quests.situationText: A furniture company has arranged to deliver your wardrobe on Wednesday morning. You'll be at work, and you'll be home on Thursday afternoon. You're on the phone with them.
quests.sampleAnswer: Hello, I'd like to change my delivery to Thursday afternoon, if that's possible. I won't be home in the morning.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to move my delivery to Thursday afternoon, if possible. I won't be home in the morning.
acceptedSynonyms: Could you rearrange my delivery for Thursday afternoon? Nobody will be there Wednesday morning.
I'd like to move my delivery to Thursday afternoon, if possible. I won't be home in the morning.
Would it be possible to deliver on Thursday afternoon instead? I can't be in on Wednesday morning.
I need to change my delivery time. Thursday afternoon would work better for me.
